claims.text: The untreated (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a large caloric response under applied magnetic-field and pressure-field operation.
The untreated alloy has poor mechanical integrity and tends to crack under mechanical loading.
The as-prepared alloy has a coarse microstructure.
The as-prepared alloy contains heterogeneous phases that cause its poor integrity and cracking.
Severe plastic deformation introduces high dislocation densities.
Severe plastic deformation fragments and refines the grains.
Annealing after severe plastic deformation can produce partial to near-full recrystallization, depending on the annealing schedule.
The proposed treatment will produce a uniformly refined, fine-grained microstructure in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
Optimized annealing will form a homogeneous dispersion of small, ductile precipitates in the target alloy.
The proposed ductile precipitates will arrest crack initiation and propagation.
The SPD-and-annealing treatment will increase the target alloy's compressive, tensile, and yield strengths relative to the untreated alloy.
The treatment will increase ductility and toughness relative to the untreated alloy.
The treatment will improve resistance to cracking, including under cyclic loading.
The tailored microstructure will leave the phase transformation responsible for the caloric effect substantially unaltered.
The caloric response after treatment will differ from that of the untreated alloy by less than 5% under identical field and temperature conditions.
The predicted benefits will hold across magnetic fields, pressure fields, temperatures, and mechanical loads representative of device operation.
Prior work on other medium- and high-entropy alloys supports microstructural and mechanical changes from severe plastic deformation and annealing.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts a uniformly recrystallized microstructure, whereas the intervention explicitly targets anything from partial to near-full recrystallization; a partially recrystallized state is not necessarily uniformly recrystallized.
